title: Floating micro‑quota fairness and interday carve‑out for reserved pools
creator: Marco Rodriguez
description:
Background: Reserved capacity customers occasionally encounter unfair early depletion when their tenant traffic is bursty across UTC boundaries or when rolling reset windows overlap with scheduled warmups. Prior tickets have focused on deterministic resets and epoch anchoring, but we still see cross-day fairness issues for customers on monthly quotas and for linked tenants that share reserved pools.

Goal: Implement a floating micro-quota layer and an interday carve-out mechanism that: 1) preserves monthly bucket guarantees for reserved customers, 2) prevents short-term eviction of long-running flows during global midnight boundaries, and 3) remains backward-compatible with existing lease and reset semantics. Deliver a rollout plan, telemetry to validate fairness, and a rollback strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce floating micro-quota token buckets per-tenant that can borrow up to X% of next-epoch allocation without triggering billing overages
Interday carve-out prevents tenant eviction for requests that start before epoch boundary and complete within a configurable grace window
No change to existing billing invoices for customers who do not opt into soft borrowing (default off)
Integration tests covering timezone-crossing requests, tenant-linking, and reserved-pool preemption scenarios
Prometheus and traces show <1% increase in  p99 latency and <3% token accounting drift during canary rollout
Rollback can be executed by toggling a feature-flag and reconciling micro-quota counters to main ledger within 24 hours
design_decisions: Use a soft-borrow semaphore: micro-quotas are fungible per-tenant and reconciled to main ledger at checkpoint, minimizing heavy-weight ledger writes
Grace window default set to 300 seconds for interday carve-out; configurable per-tenant with reserved accounts having longer grace by policy
Adopt conservative default soft-borrow rate of 10% of monthly allocation to limit cost exposure; allow enterprise customers to set higher via contract
Telemetry-first rollout: implement detailed delta metrics before enabling enforcement paths
Avoid introducing new persistent schema changes in the main usage ledger; keep micro-quota state as compact shards stored with TTL for easy prune
implementation_notes: Runtime: add a microQuota layer in front of the quota allocator; check main quota, then microQuota borrow path, then reservation fallback
Atomicity: use optimistic compare-and-swap on tenant lease tokens to ensure idempotent borrow and reconciliation
Reconciliation: nightly checkpoint job aggregates micro-borrows and issues internal ledger adjustments tied to tenant epoch
Migration: for tenants with active reserved contracts, seed microQuota allowances based on last 3 months usage percentile
Edge cases: long-running streaming requests must attach a start-timestamp; carve-out applies if start_ts < epoch_boundary + grace_window
rollout_plan: Developer proof-of-concept branch with unit tests (ENG-100101-poc)
Internal canary: enable for 5 internal test tenants for 48 hours; validate telemetry and billing neutrality
Limited external canary: opt-in beta for three reserved customers under SE supervision for one week
Gradual ramp: increase to 20% reserved pool capacity over two weeks while monitoring failure rates and token drift
Full roll: flip global feature flag for reserved pools after 4 weeks of stable telemetry; run reconciliation job within 24h
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Underestimated borrow rate causes effective overprovisioning and higher infra cost. Mitigation: conservative defaults and per-tenant caps; billing guardrails to prevent invoice surprises.
Risk: Reconciliation race causes double-counting. Mitigation: idempotent checkpoints and event-sourced tombstones for reconciled micro-borrows.
Risk: Unexpected latency regressions in hot path. Mitigation: precompute small constant-time checks and push heavy reconciliation off hot path.
Risk: Cross-region clock skew affects grace-window logic. Mitigation: use canonical UTC epoch from central control plane and versioned leases.
qa_notes: Create synthetic traffic generator that simulates timezone-crossing bursts and long-lived streams
Add regression tests for midnight boundary handling and tenant-link preemption scenarios
Coordinate with billing to run invoice dry-runs for beta tenants to validate zero-impact default
